note: Device-level guidance from Apple's public support articles. Used as a second tier after MultiTracks' Playback documentation: for the device, OS, network, storage, and audio-routing layers that Playback articles point to but do not explain.

articles.title: How to check the storage on your iPhone and iPad
articles.summary: Where to see how full the device is, which apps use the most space, and how to free space. Relevant when Playback reports Insufficient Storage or downloads fail on a nearly full device.
steps: Open Settings, tap General, then tap iPad Storage (or iPhone Storage) to see how much space is free and which apps use the most.
If the device shows Storage Almost Full, tap Show All on the Storage screen and review Apple's recommendations, such as offloading unused apps.
Remove large items you no longer need, such as videos or unused apps, then try the download in Playback again.

articles.title: If you can't connect to Wi-Fi on your iPhone or iPad
articles.summary: Checks for the device's network connection, from Wi-Fi settings to VPN software and the router. Relevant when downloads fail or stall, or Playback can't reach the cloud.
steps: Go to Settings, then Wi-Fi, make sure Wi-Fi is on and a checkmark shows next to your network. Also check that Airplane Mode is off.
Check whether other devices can get online on the same network. If they can't, the problem is the network rather than the iPad.
If a VPN or security app is installed, turn it off or remove it, restart the device, and test again.
Move closer to the router, and if it offers both bands try the 5 gigahertz network instead of 2.4.
Restart the router and modem by unplugging them and plugging them back in.
Last resort: Settings, General, Transfer or Reset, Reset, Reset Network Settings. This erases saved Wi-Fi networks and passwords, so check with IT first on a church or business network.

articles.title: If an app on your iPhone or iPad stops responding, closes unexpectedly, or won't open
articles.summary: Apple's general sequence for an app that misbehaves: force close, restart the device, update, then reinstall.
steps: Force close the app, then reopen it: swipe up from the bottom of the screen and pause, then swipe the app's preview up.
Restart the iPhone or iPad, then open the app again.
Open the App Store, tap your profile icon, and check App Updates for an update to the app. If none is listed, update the device's software.
Delete the app and reinstall it from the App Store. This can erase data stored in the app, so only do it when there's time to set it up again.

articles.title: Allow USB and other accessories to connect to your iPhone or iPad
articles.summary: The Wired Accessories security setting controls whether a USB device, such as an audio interface, can connect while the device is locked or before it's approved.
steps: Unlock the iPad or iPhone, then unplug and reconnect the USB cable or adapter. If a prompt asks to allow the accessory, tap Allow.
Check the setting: Settings, Privacy and Security, then Wired Accessories under Security. Automatically Allow When Unlocked is the default; Always Allow lets accessories connect while locked.

articles.title: Charge and connect with the USB-C port on your iPad
articles.summary: The iPad's USB-C port works with audio interfaces, hubs and docks, and USB-C headphones. Other speakers or headphones need Apple's USB-C to 3.5 mm adapter. Some accessories draw more power from the iPad.
steps: Confirm the connection type: USB-C audio interfaces and hubs plug straight into the iPad's USB-C port; speakers or headphones with a 3.5 millimeter plug need Apple's USB-C to 3.5 mm adapter.
If the interface or hub draws power from the iPad, connect it through a powered hub or dock so it has its own power.

articles.title: If you hear no sound or distorted sound from your iPhone, iPad, or iPod touch speaker
articles.summary: Device-level checks when nothing comes out of the built-in speaker: Silent mode, Do Not Disturb, blocked openings, and a speaker test.
steps: Make sure Silent mode is off: on iPad, swipe down from the top-right corner to open Control Center and check the Silent mode button; on older iPhones, check the Ring/Silent switch.
Turn off Do Not Disturb: Settings, Focus, Do Not Disturb.
Test the speaker: Settings, Sounds, and drag the Ringtone and Alerts slider. If you hear nothing, the device speaker may need service, and an external output is the workaround.

articles.title: If your headphones don't work with your iPhone or iPad
articles.summary: Checks for wired headphones or a headphone-port cable: port debris, cable damage, a firm connection, volume, and a second pair to isolate the fault.
steps: Check the headphone port for lint or debris, and inspect the cable and connector for damage.
Reconnect firmly, removing the case if it stops the plug seating fully, then raise the volume with the side buttons or Control Center.
Try a second pair of headphones or a different cable. If the second one works, the first cable or pair is the problem.

articles.title: If a Bluetooth accessory won't connect to your iPhone or iPad
articles.summary: Apple's steps for a Bluetooth speaker, headphones, or pedal that won't connect. Playback's documentation does not cover Bluetooth outputs, so this is device-level guidance only.
steps: Keep the accessory close to the device, turn it off and back on, and make sure it's charged.
If the accessory was paired before, forget it in Settings, Bluetooth, then put it back in pairing mode and pair it again.
If it works with other devices but not this one, unpair it from those devices and pair it with this iPad or iPhone again.

articles.title: Change the sound output settings on Mac
articles.summary: How to choose which device the Mac sends sound to and check volume, mute, and balance.
steps: Choose Apple menu, System Settings, then Sound. Click Output and select the device you want, such as your audio interface.
Check that the Output volume slider isn't all the way down and that Mute is not selected. Also check the Balance slider is centered.

articles.title: If you can't hear sound from your Mac speakers
articles.summary: Mac checks when there's no sound: app volume, the selected output, and whether a USB device is detected.
steps: Check the app's own volume isn't muted, and try a different audio source to see whether the problem is the Mac or the app.
For a USB interface or USB speakers: select it in System Settings, Sound, Output.
Check the Mac sees the USB device: hold Option, choose Apple menu, System Information, then click USB under Hardware. If it isn't listed, unplug and reconnect it.

articles.title: Set up audio devices in Audio MIDI Setup on Mac
articles.summary: Audio MIDI Setup sets an interface's format and sample rate and its speaker configuration. Playback's documentation does not cover sample rate; this is the macOS-level setting.
steps: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications, Utilities) and select the interface in the sidebar.
Use the Format pop-up to choose a sample rate and bit depth that match the audio interface.
To make it the default output, Control-click the interface and choose Use This Device for Sound Output.

articles.title: If you can't find or use your Apple In-App Purchases
articles.summary: What to check when an in-app subscription isn't recognized: restore from inside the app, confirm the Apple Account, check purchases are allowed, restart.
steps: Use the app's own restore option. In Playback that's Settings, About, Restore Purchases.
If restoring does nothing, confirm the device is signed in to the same Apple Account that bought the subscription.
Restart the device, then try Restore Purchases again.

articles.title: Update your iPhone or iPad
articles.summary: How to check the device's iOS or iPadOS version and install an update. Relevant when the device is below the app's minimum OS version.
steps: Check the device's version: Settings, General, Software Update shows the current iOS or iPadOS version and whether an update is available.
To update, back up first, plug in, connect to Wi-Fi, then tap Download and Install. This restarts the device, so it's not for during a service.
